subject: Eval to Contract: ramp plan & commercial milestones
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Eval to Contract: ramp plan & commercial milestones

Hi Laura —

Great to meet you on Wednesday. Per our call, attaching a first-draft mutual action plan (MAP) for the 4-week evaluation. High level:

- Week 0 (kickoff): access + sample data ingest; Redwood provides 5000 token pilot credits to validate latency and quality.
- Week 1–2 (integration): SDK integration, routing and caching tests; we recommend the "balanced" quantization profile to match performance targets.
- Week 3 (stress): throughput tests at 200 TPS simulated; we provide guidance on batching policy.
- Week 4 (acceptance): run your acceptance prompt set; success = <2% regression on key prompts and latency SLOs met.

Commercial asks tied to MAP milestones: if Finlytics signs a 12-month Dedicated commit within 30 days of acceptance, Redwood will convert pilot credits into a $15k credit toward the first invoice and lock the quoted EFU-based price for 6 months. If you need more time, we can extend pilot credits conditionally per the notes below.

Attached: MAP_v1.pdf (draft), SOW_draft.docx (template).

Next steps: please confirm the acceptance criteria and procurement timeline. If procurement needs a PO path, loop Tom and I can get finance involved.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172
[Attachment: MAP_v1.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]
[Attachment: SOW_draft.docx (DOCX, 22KB)]

From: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@finlytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval to Contract: ramp plan & commercial milestones

Thanks Mina — this looks close to what we discussed. Quick clarifying questions before we send to procurement: 

- The 5000 token pilot credits — is that per-user, per-organization, or total pool? We need to quote that to our budget owner.
- If we sign the 12-month commit within 30 days, does the $15k credit apply against the first invoice only, or can it offset implementation fees?
- What happens if our acceptance test shows a regression of 2–4%? Is there a remediation window?

Procurement's calendar is tight in September; we may need an extra week on the evaluation to complete security review. Tom, can procurement prioritize or should we request a short extension from Redwood?

— Laura
Senior Product Manager, Finlytics
laura.cheng@finlytics.com | +1 212-555-0118

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@finlytics.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval to Contract: ramp plan & commercial milestones

Laura — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and an updated commercial note below.

- Pilot credits: these are a shared org-level pool for the POC. We can track usage per project in the console but the 5000 tokens are a total pool for the trial unless you ask for a larger allocation.
- Credit application: the $15k converts to a contract credit and can be applied to first invoice line items (invoiced usage or implementation work) — we treat implementation discounts on a case-by-case basis but will honor up to $5k against SOW services.
- Acceptance regression: if regression is between 0–2% we consider it pass. 2–5% triggers a remediation plan (1 week of joint work; Redwood engineers to tune prompts/config). >5% requires a joint review and may affect the conversion credit until resolved.

Updated conditional extension offer (commercial):
- If procurement needs +7 calendar days to complete security & PO approval, Redwood will add an incremental 2500 token credit pool (one-time) provided: (a) Finlytics confirms intent to convert (non-binding) and (b) signs the MAP signature page by 2026-09-22.
- If conversion does not occur within 60 days post-acceptance, the $15k credit expires.

Attaching an annotated pricing_sheet.xlsx that maps commits to EFU tiers and the proposed Dedicated ramp (50k tokens/mo initial -> scale to 300k tokens/mo over 6 months).

Ben Carter
Head of Mid-Market Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
[Attachment: pricing_sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 14KB)]

On Fri, Aug 27, 2026 at 11:28 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Laura — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and an updated commercial note below.

Appreciate the clarity. Procurement can prioritize but will need the MAP signed and a short statement of work to process any PO. Two practical asks from our side: 

1) Can you push the acceptance window to 5 weeks (we need internal QA/SME time) or provide a mid-eval checkpoint that counts toward acceptance?
2) If we take the +7 day extension now, can you confirm there will be no changes to the locked EFU price during that window?

If both are yes, I can commit to moving this through legal and finance next week.

Thanks — Tom
VP, Platform Engineering, Finlytics
[Finlytics internal note: procurement lead is Janet Park; PO path requires SOW + vendor W-9]

- Acceptance window: we will accept a 5-week evaluation window (midpoint checkpoint at end of week 3) and treat the midpoint as a go/no-go input to acceptance.
- Extension credit & price lock: we will add the +2500 token top-up (as Ben outlined) if Finlytics signs the MAP signature page by 2026-09-22. The quoted EFU price is locked for that signature window and will not change.
- SOW/PO path: attached SOW_draft.docx is ready for your procurement; Rishi from finance is on copy to expedite PO questions and confirm the credit mechanics. Once MAP signature is received, we'll issue a short confirmation and a DocuSign link for the SOW.
